title: Leading Lottie Hightower and Her Nighthawks in Chicago
summary: After quitting Carroll Dickerson's band he built his own, worked six and a half years on the Gold Coast, and sorted out the Nighthawks name with Joe Sanders and Coon.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, Baby was working with me at the entertainers. Well, he got me the job over there, see, with Carol Dixon. Well, I didn't care for it very much so I just quit that altogether and I wanted to build my band myself. So I just went to work and bought a car and went out on the north side and went around places and advertised the band. Finally, we got out of my work, we got six years and a half work of the band on the Gold Coast and over Chicago with the band under her name. The band never was under my name. After I found it in her night, Eudora Nighthawks. Eudora came from a dancing class, was at Fortis and State. That was Mason Hall. And the man that used to run dancing classes here in Chicago. Every night in the week there was a dancing class somewhere. Well, he had shows, he put on shows and he would get jobs like at Congress Hotel, Eudora Beach Hotel and all them places. He'd take 45 and 50 people. He was like Joneses with the choir around here, you know, take a big bunch of, yeah. And then he built a band right along with it. And they helped both him and what we did, we named the band Lolly Hightower and Eudora Nighthawks band. Coincidence that happened, after we had that name going, Joe Saunders and Dale Coon come in here with the Nighthawks. Oh sure, yeah. They come to St. Louis. And he says that he had had the name for a long time. Well, we didn't squabble over it at all. We met out here at 35th and State Street one night and went in a restaurant and sat down and talked. Well, Joe Saunders was kind of a hard fellow to talk with, but Dale Coon was all right. Dale Coon was the drummer, see. Well, he was a pretty good fellow. Joe Saunders was the piano player.
Yeah, we could hear him already.
